Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the StratoCloud Q2 FY25 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register using the *1 and *2 keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing StratoCloud's results for the Q2 FY25. With me on the call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Liam Chen, Chief Technology Officer; Sophia Grant, Chief Product Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Marketing Officer; Taylor Brooks, Chief Sales Officer; and Dr. Nadia Patel, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. StratoCloud continued its strong growth trajectory in the Q2 FY25, driven by robust demand for our comprehensive suite of cloud services and solutions.

During the quarter, our key priorities included:
1. Expanding our presence in emerging markets.
2. Accelerating the adoption of our AI-powered platform.
3. Enhancing our developer ecosystem.
4. Strengthening our commitment to sustainability.
5. Investing in employee training and development.
6. Improving cross-functional collaboration.
7. Ensuring the security and privacy of our customers' data.

We saw exceptional momentum across our IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS offerings, including StratoCompute for high-performance computing, StratoAI for generative AI workloads, and StratoEdge for hybrid multi-cloud edge deployments. Total revenue came in at $6.7 billion, up 28% year-over-year, surpassing our prior guidance and reflecting the strength of our land-and-expand model amid surging AI demand.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. We are pleased to report another quarter of strong financial results. Revenue grew by 28% year-over-year to $6.7 billion, exceeding our guidance range of $6.4 billion to $6.6 billion by about 2%. This marks our 15th straight quarter of accelerating growth, outpacing the industry's 21% to 25% pace as reported by Gartner and IDC for cloud infrastructure. Our gross margin expanded to 73%, up over 200 basis points year-over-year, driven by a favorable mix shift toward high-margin AI services. Operating margin reached 32%, reflecting efficient scaling and operating leverage.

Let me unpack the key drivers behind this performance, starting with total revenue details. For Q2 ended June 30, 2025, we delivered $6.7 billion, beating the high end of our Q1 guide by $500 million or roughly 2%. This outperformance stemmed from accelerated consumption in AI/ML workloads, which now make up 28% of revenue, up from 22% last year, and quicker ramps from our top enterprise customers committing to sovereign cloud setups. IaaS led with $3.8 billion, up 32% year-over-year, powered by Graviton4 ARM instances offering 25% better price-performance and massive NVIDIA H100 GPU clusters averaging over 10,000 GPUs per deployment, akin to builds at Meta and OpenAI. PaaS and data services contributed $2.1 billion, growing 25%, with StratoKube Kubernetes adoption up 40% and StratoDB capturing 15% cloud-native database share per IDC. SaaS rounded out at $1.8 billion, up 22%, boosted by zero-trust security and sustainability tools.

Year-over-year, this 28% growth beat industry averages, fueled by AI tailwinds where inference now outpaces training at 4:1 ratios, enterprise multi-cloud at 68% penetration among top customers, and cost efficiencies like PUE at 1.18 and 65% renewables. Regions showed balance: Americas at 62% mix with 29% growth from financials and healthcare; EMEA 22% with 25% on GDPR zones; APAC 16% fastest at 32% via Tokyo expansions and India ramps.

Turning to average revenue per customer, or ARPU, which we calculate as annualized recurring revenue divided by average monthly active accounts, excluding one-time services to highlight sticky cloud streams. Q2 ARPU hit $142,000, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, with full-year average at $138,500, surpassing peer growth of 12-15%. Enterprise customers over $1M ACV, 42% of revenue, drove 28% ARPU growth to $478,000 via AI GPU expansions; mid-market at $89,000 up 15% on edge and PaaS; SMBs at $12,500 up 8%. Product mix lifted it, with AI/ML adding $22,000, data analytics $18,000, core IaaS $65,000. Regionally, North America $156,000 up 20%, EMEA $112,000 up 16%, APAC $98,000 up 25%. Net retention at 118-122%, dollar retention 92%, RPO tied to expansions up 31%. Looking ahead, we see 15-18% growth from AI bundles, enterprise focus, developer tools, and committed-use discounts.

Speaking of visibility, Remaining Performance Obligations, or RPO, ended the quarter at $48.2 billion, up 32% year-over-year and 9% sequentially. Current RPO within 12 months at $22.4 billion, up 28% YoY and 11% QoQ, backed by 128% dollar-based net retention with 40% from AI add-ons like StratoAI Studio. Non-current RPO at $25.8 billion, up 36%, mostly from $10M+ ACV customers on 3-5 year sovereign deals. cRPO is 46.5% of total, with average contracts at 38 months. North America 62% up 35%, EMEA up 42% to $12.1B on Frankfurt/Paris zones, APAC up 45% to $9.8B on edge AI. AI drove 55% growth, land-and-expand added $3.2B, new logos ACV up 22%. This banks 115% of full-year guide, covering 2.1x FY26 expectations.

Currency fluctuations impacted us as a global player with 55% international revenue. FX headwinds deducted $285 million, or 4.2%, from Q2 results at constant currency, worsening from Q2's 3.1%, due to USD strength. YoY, it cut growth by 180bps; constant currency was 31% up. EMEA took $140M hit from 9% euro drop, still 35% cc growth; APAC $95M from yen/AUD, 30% cc; LatAm $50M from real. Mitigations include 75% hedge coverage buffering $115M, local-currency pricing in 85% markets, and diversification to India/Singapore hubs. Q3 expect $300-350M headwind, easing to 2-3% next year.

Our forecasts rest on solid assumptions. Revenue guide assumes 118-122% NRR, 12-15% new logos, compute/AI 35% growth on H100 clusters, storage 18%, databases 28%, PaaS 22%. Americas 24%, EMEA 20%, APAC 38%. AI capex steady, pricing neutral, 5% FX drag. Gross margins to 73% FY25 on capex efficiency, PUE 1.15, custom silicon; op margins 32% with S&M 22%, R&D 18%; FCF 25%. Sensitivities model bull/bear cases around AI TAM to $200B by 2027.

Finally, on cloud services gross margins at 73.2%, up 210bps YoY. Mix shift to 28% AI at premium pricing drove most, with PaaS/SaaS at 78-85%. COGS up from $4.2B capex, D&A 18%, power 15% higher, but Graviton4 at 82% utilization, liquid cooling, 60% renewables countered. Americas 76%, APAC 70%, EMEA 68%. Savings plans at 65%, dynamic GPU pricing add uplift. Expect 74-75% FY25, 77% FY26.

Before Q&A, we're raising FY25 revenue guidance to $32.5 billion to $34.0 billion, 26-31% growth at midpoint, beating prior $31-32.5B and Street by 2%. Q3 $8.4-8.6B, up 28-31% QoQ. IaaS $18.5-19.5B at 30-34%, PaaS $9.2-9.8B at 24-29%, SaaS $4.8-5.0B at 22-26%. Regions: Americas ~$20.5B 29%, EMEA $7.5B 25%, APAC $5.5B 32%. $10B capex on AI DCs, NVIDIA ties, Saudi JV. Assumes stable GPU supply, no macro downturn.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Liam Chen, who will provide an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Liam Chen:
Thank you, Marcus. We are making significant investments in research and development to stay at the forefront of cloud innovation. We are particularly excited about our progress in AI-powered platforms and confidential computing.

Our Graviton4 instances and StratoAI Accelerator with NVIDIA H100/H200 GPUs are scaling massive clusters, while StratoKube and StratoDB drive migrations. We've improved PUE to 1.18, renewables to 65%, and advanced edge AI with 5G integrations. Custom silicon like AMD SEV-SNP reduces costs 40%, positioning us for quantum-safe crypto and exabyte data lakes.

Now, I'll pass it to Sophia Grant for a product update.

Sophia Grant:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We recently launched StratoAI Accelerator, which is already gaining significant traction in the market.

This builds on StratoEdge for hybrid deployments and Nebula-like inference engines, with zero-ETL pipelines and vector DBs rivaling Snowflake Cortex. Adoption is strong in FinOps, sovereign zones, and GenAI fine-tuning, shortening cycles and boosting attach rates to 45%.

I'll now hand it over to Jordan Lee to discuss our marketing strategy.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Sophia. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions.

We're emphasizing AI sovereignty, multi-cloud interoperability with Azure Arc and Anthos, and sustainability for CSRD compliance. Campaigns target hyperscalers in financials, healthcare, and telcos, driving 40% lead growth in APAC and EMEA via developer free tiers and partner ecosystems.

Next, I'd like to introduce Taylor Brooks, who will provide an update on our sales performance.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jordan. Our sales team delivered a strong performance in the Q2 FY25, driven by increased customer adoption of our cloud services.

We signed 15 seven-figure deals in Americas, expanded in Japan/India with SoftBank analogs, and hit 128% NRR. Enterprise wallet share up 20%, new logos ACV $4.5M, with AI upsells at 35% attach.

Finally, I'll pass it to Dr. Nadia Patel to discuss our security initiatives.

Dr. Nadia Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. Security is our top priority. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and maintaining the highest standards of security.

Our zero-trust suite grew 35%, FedRAMP High and GDPR zones ensure sovereignty, confidential computing with SGX/SEV-SNP protects workloads, and ransomware defenses align with EUCS.

Back to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator:
Our first question comes from Sarah Kline with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kline:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. On the raised FY25 guidance to $32.5-34B, can you elaborate on segment and regional assumptions, especially AI mix and CapEx allocation?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Sarah. Yes, the raise reflects AI inference ramps, with 28% mix now and inference:training at 4:1 boosting recurring pay-go. IaaS leads at 30-34% to $18.5-19.5B on 85% utilization and H100 clusters; PaaS 24-29%, SaaS 22-26%. Americas 29% on hyperscalers, APAC 32% fastest. $10B CapEx, 30% up, targets Virginia/Osaka/Sydney AI DCs, with 80% H200 secured.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Torres with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Torres:
Great, thanks. On gross margins at 73.2% and FX headwinds, how are you mitigating COGS inflation and what’s the constant currency view for Q3 revenue?

Marcus Hale:
Thanks, Mike. Margins expanded on AI mix at 2-3x premium, Graviton4 efficiencies, and 82% utilization despite $4.2B CapEx. Power up 15% but PUE 1.18 and 60% renewables offset; liquid cooling pilots target 1.10. FX shaved 4.2% this quarter, hedged 75% for $115M gain; Q3 cc revenue implies 31% growth in guide. Dynamic pricing and 65% savings plans sustain 74-75% FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Rao with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Priya Rao:
Thank you. Impressive RPO at $48.2B and ARPU up 18%. What’s driving the 128% NRR, and any updates on multi-year contract trends?

Dr. Liam Chen:
Thanks, Priya. RPO growth, with cRPO $22.4B up 28%, ties to 128% NRR from AI add-ons like StratoAI Studio at 3-5x upsizes and 85% stickiness in $10M+ deals averaging 38 months now. ARPU levers include GenAI bundles at 145% growth and edge PaaS; expansions added $3.2B this quarter. Tech like ForgeML with Ray and zero-ETL shortens cycles, supporting 28-32% CAGR.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your questions. We appreciate your continued support.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
